plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub native to Mexico with showy colored bracts surrounding small yellow flower clusters called cyathia. In its native range and in warm climates it blooms outdoors, and it is widely grown as a potted plant elsewhere for the holidays.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February)
plants.location: Native to Mexico and Central America; cultivated worldwide, outdoors in USDA zones 9-11
plants.funFact: The colorful parts are modified leaves called bracts, not petals. The plant needs about 12 hours of uninterrupted darkness each night for roughly 8 weeks to color up, and the Aztecs used it to make a reddish dye.

plants.name: Hippeastrum hybrids
plants.description: A bulbous plant with trumpet-shaped flowers up to 25 cm across on tall hollow stalks. Bulbs forced indoors in the Northern Hemisphere bloom around the holidays, while in the Southern Hemisphere garden plants flower naturally in the early summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter indoors in the Northern Hemisphere; late spring to early summer outdoors in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America (Andes and Brazil); cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: The bulb contains enough stored energy that it can flower with no soil or water, and a mature bulb may send up two or more flower stalks in a season.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: An evergreen perennial with strap-like leaves and large round umbels of funnel-shaped flowers on tall stems. It is at its peak in the Southern Hemisphere summer, with blooms lasting several weeks.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (December to February in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South Africa; widely planted in Australia, New Zealand, and Mediterranean-climate regions
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, it is not a true lily. The name comes from Greek words meaning love flower, and it thrives in coastal gardens because it tolerates salt spray.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers, among the most beloved winter bloomers in temperate regions. Early cultivars open in December and bloom through early spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring (December to March in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and eastern China; grown in the southeastern United States, Europe, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Tea is made from a close relative, Camellia sinensis, and camellia oil from the seeds of Camellia japonica has long been used in Japan for hair care and cooking.
